metrics.outcome: Done: the site is workable. Every done-when item passes with Audit's evidence and the render check is clean.
metrics.brief: make a website for my cousin's clothing boutique called Thread & Loom in Pune. it sells handloom kurtas, sarees, cotton shirts and dupattas. people should be able to browse products by category, filter by size and price, see a size guide, check new arrivals, and order on whatsapp. also show a lookbook section with styled outfits, the store timings and location, the return and exchange policy, and a few customer reviews. it should feel earthy and elegant and work well on phones

estimate_vs_charged.name: Product catalogue with filters and WhatsApp order

review.verdict: The department delivered a workable site in 2 cycles at 177 of 200 with no invalid moves, but nobody clicked the filters or order links, and this brief never tested negotiation, conflict or lessons.

identity.note: Two focused question rounds [2][5], honest hand-off to the Requester that names the two warnings and asks for a phone check [51]. Slight overreach: [38] dictates the CSS fix (font, radius) instead of just naming the defect.

adaptation.note: Seven workflows covering all 14 items inside budget [11], and a tight 2-workflow rework [39]. Never set page order, which caused the cycle-1 hero defect. The trade-off sentence in [39] is garbled.

priority.note: Stayed in role. Both GRANTs matched the ask, with a reserve kept [12][40]. It accepted 24 for one hero move because pricing was per finding. Only 2 of its 11 turns look like real decisions (inferred: the 9 envelope checks are identical templates).

coordination.note: Stated its scheduling rule every time, with no collisions and no holds. But [26][32] tell builders what content must say, which is outside its role. Rule text is duplicated with stray '..' in [23][29].

audit.note: Caught both real defects in cycle 1 [37], confirmed the fixes [50], and said plainly that filters were checked by reading logic only. Its chat never names the two warnings; F-10 is item 10, the lookbook (inferred).

W-1.note: Clean shell and shared ids. But the nav hides links to missing ids [16], which can hide a missing section from the broken-link check.

W-2.note: Contact and timings correct [22]. The hero ended up after the shop through no fault of its own.

W-3.note: 10 cards, combined filters, wa.me links [19]. Shipped the Clear filters font defect (F-16), and the order buttons have square corners [51].

W-4.note: Exact chest values, two columns for 360px [25].

W-5.note: Three correct products with names and prices [28].

W-6.note: Outfit 2 is one saree and only 5 of 10 products are used [31][51]. Meets the letter of the check, not the intent.

W-7.note: Policy, delivery and reviews match the brief [34].

W-8.note: Hero moves ahead of the shop by a script with a CSS fallback [44]. It works but is fragile. It was forced into this by the section-order limit and it named the fallback.

W-9.note: Minimal, scoped fix that left filter logic alone [47].

went_well: All 14 done-when items pass, with a clean mechanical check at 360px and 1280px [49][50].
0 redirects and 0 invalid moves across about 38 turns; no scope creep.
Every builder and Audit said what was not verified, and Identity passed that on to the Requester [51].
The rework was targeted: 2 small workflows, 32 money, 23 left.
problems: Hero after shop in cycle 1 cost a cycle and 32 money because no one owned page order [37][39].
Nothing was run in a browser. Filters and WhatsApp links were checked by reading code only [19][37][50].
Shipped with 2 known warnings (single-saree outfit, square order buttons) while 23 was unspent [51].
The broken-link check can be satisfied by W-1 hiding the link [16][36].
learnings: Test system: add a headless click test (category plus size plus price combined, and each wa.me href). Without it, 'workable' rests on reading code. Evidence: [19][50].
Test system: rerun with a budget near 100 so Priority must COUNTER or REFUSE. This run had 0 counters, 0 refusals, 0 conflicts and 0 holds, so the bargaining and conflict paths are untested.
Test system: turn lessons memory on. It was off (saved: [], used: []), so the save-a-lesson step could not be judged.

Test system: estimate equals charge on all 9 workflows (rate card), so cost-estimating skill is unmeasurable. Rate card charges per finding, not effort (24 for one move [40]); consider pricing by work.
J2 design: make page order part of W-1's shell contract or the charter. Keep splitting by section, since it caused no collisions.
J2 design: make the Audit warning list visible in chat. Also reconcile audit.md (defects to Adaptation) with team.md (everything to Identity).
Evidence is thin on visual quality: 'earthy and elegant' was judged only by code measurements.
